clue.text: Annoyed by article on greed being broadcast

parts.note: the indefinite article before a vowel

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is irritated by a newspaper piece about greed that has gone out on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a person who has been made cross or irritated; they are straightforward synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Gratification found in prayer certainly

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request or entreaty
'sure!' is a casual way of saying certainly

explanation.surface: A believer finds satisfaction in prayer, without a doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratification is the feeling of enjoyment or satisfaction when a desire is met, which is what this noun names.

clue.text: Voting to stand behind a dancing event

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: in a down entry, a word made to stand upright is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A candidate for election is asked to queue at the back of a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' places the upended word after the dance in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballot is a process of secret voting, so the noun stands in for voting as an activity, a slightly loose synonym.

clue.text: Not all rest uneasily in the West Country

definitions.note: the answer is one county within the West Country, so this is definition by example with 'in'

parts.note: some means part but not the whole

indicators.note: something resting uneasily shifts about, so these letters are moved into another order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers in south-west England do not all sleep soundly.
explanation.walkthrough: The West Country is south-west England; SOMERSET is one of its counties.
explanation.definitionFit: Somerset is a county lying in south-west England, the region the British call the West Country.

clue.text: Get the better of a schoolteacher

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to overcome or conquer, as a verb
second meaning: a male teacher, as in a schoolmaster

explanation.surface: A pupil hopes to outwit the teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to overcome or gain control; as a noun it is a traditional British title for a male teacher.

clue.text: During the ascent edelweiss is detected by smell

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A climber notices the fragrance of alpine edelweiss on the way up.
explanation.definitionFit: To have scented something is to have picked it up through the nose, as a hound does a trail.

clue.text: Indistinct nuclear explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and reformed

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A blurry image of an atomic blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unclear lacks sharpness or definition, which is exactly what indistinct describes.

clue.text: King against going in a month

indicators.note: one word going in another is placed inside it

parts.note: the third month of the year
leaning on something is resting against it

explanation.surface: A king opposes going somewhere in a particular month.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch is a sovereign ruler, and a king is the commonest example of such a crowned head of state.

clue.text: Needling someone — but it's for their own good

definitions.text: Needling someone — but it's for their own good

parts.note: surface reading: deliberately irritating or provoking a person

parts.words: but it's for their own good
parts.note: setter's reading: literally sticking fine needles into a patient as a healing treatment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Needling' looks like teasing or goading; read literally it is inserting needles, which is the Chinese therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: The treatment involves inserting thin needles into the body at set points, supposedly to benefit the patient's health.

clue.text: Remember, record half of everything

indicators.note: half of a word keeps only one of its two halves, here the front portion

parts.note: the first three of its six letters
all means the whole lot

explanation.surface: An instruction to remember and write down half of what happens.
explanation.definitionFit: To recall something is to bring it back to mind, a direct synonym for the verb remember.

clue.text: Dining after church is deceiving

indicators.note: after places the dining word second, so the church abbreviation comes first

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
dining is having a meal

explanation.surface: Someone claims that going for a meal after the church service is dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the dining after the church, so the short abbreviation leads.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheating means acting dishonestly to fool others, the same present participle sense as deceiving.

clue.text: A Parisian, married, returns the food list

indicators.note: returning means going back the way one came, so the letters run right to left

parts.note: the French feminine for 'a', as a Parisian would say it
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A married Parisian woman sends the menu back at a restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the card a restaurant hands diners, setting out the dishes available to order.

clue.text: Records attempts to make ornamental textiles

parts.note: tapes are audio or video recordings
tries are goes or efforts

explanation.surface: Someone keeps notes of repeated efforts to weave decorative fabrics.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapestries are heavy woven wall hangings with pictorial designs, made for decoration rather than wear.

clue.text: Name for plan, not A1, needs changing

parts.note: a design is a plan or scheme

indicators.note: something that needs changing must be altered, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
the digit 1 stands for the letter I it resembles

explanation.surface: A name for a scheme that is not first-rate must be altered.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 means first-class, but here it is just the letters A and I to be shuffled with 'not'.
explanation.definitionFit: A designation is the title or label given to something, so it serves as a noun meaning name.

clue.text: Rich now newly married a very slow moving creature!

indicators.note: newly means in a fresh way, so these letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A wealthy newlywed is mocked as a sluggish creature.
explanation.definitionFit: An inchworm is a caterpillar that moves by looping its body, covering ground only an inch or so at a time.

clue.text: Key worker in church?

parts.note: surface reading: an essential employee, such as a vital staff member
setter's reading: a musician who works the keys of the instrument in a church

explanation.walkthrough: 'Key worker' suggests an important employee; the question mark hints it is someone who literally works keys, at a keyboard instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This musician plays the large pipe instrument with keyboards that leads hymns in most churches.

clue.text: Teleprompter Cousteau moved without first submerging

indicators.note: letters that are moved are shifted into different positions
without means lacking, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: the French undersea explorer's name taken as written

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter only of the next word

parts.note: the initial letter

explanation.surface: Jacques Cousteau needs a script screen while presenting, but not when he is diving.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one S from the name before rearranging. Autocue is the British trade name for a teleprompter.
explanation.definitionFit: Autocue is a brand name, used generically in Britain, for the screen device that shows a presenter their script.

clue.text: Suddenly frighten the French — begin to go ahead!

indicators.note: going ahead means leading, so the word for begin is placed in front of the French article

parts.note: to start is to begin
the French masculine word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A command to scare the French by getting started with an advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go ahead' tells you the word for begin goes in front of the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: To startle someone is to give them a sudden shock or fright, so the phrase is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: Built, raced, reassembled and greased

indicators.note: something reassembled is put back together in a different way, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A racing car is built, driven, taken apart and rebuilt, then oiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Lubricated means treated with oil or grease to reduce friction, so it matches greased in sense and tense.

clue.text: Soften some more lentils

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters are a portion of the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: soak extra pulses until tender.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to become less severe or strict, a figurative sense of softening one's attitude.

clue.text: Physician uses entrance outside court

indicators.note: one thing outside another wraps around it, holding it within

parts.note: a door is a way in
CT is the standard abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A doctor goes in by a door that is outside the courthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor is a qualified medical practitioner, and physician is the formal word for one who treats illness.

clue.text: Nougat emporium has hidden entrance

indicators.note: something hidden lies concealed inside, so the letters are tucked within those words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A sweet shop selling nougat has a concealed way in.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is a hinged barrier forming a way into a field, garden or yard, so it serves as an entrance.

clue.text: One not going before finding a disciple?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who comes behind rather than leading
second meaning: an adherent of a teacher or cause

explanation.surface: Someone who hangs back discovers a devoted pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it is one who comes after; figuratively it is a supporter or adherent of a leader, as disciples were.

clue.text: Can a miniature railway get one flying?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a miniature railway is the word cut down: RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A question whether a small model train can take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miniature' does not mean a toy train: it shrinks the word railway to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A canary is a small yellow songbird, so it is something that flies; the definition is deliberately vague.

clue.text: Women must be ordered to live in one

definitions.text: Women must be ordered to live in one

parts.note: surface reading: women being commanded or told what to do
setter's reading: women belonging to a religious order reside in this kind of house

explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' seems to mean commanded, but it means belonging to a religious order, like the sisters who live together.
explanation.definitionFit: A convent is home to sisters who have taken vows in a religious order, and only they reside there.

clue.text: Initially carried on part of foot for comfort

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the initial letter
taken as written
the sole is the underside of the foot

explanation.surface: Someone first kept walking on the sole of the foot to ease the pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to give them solace in grief or disappointment, the verb sense of comfort.
